segments.text: I want to quickly bring in Advaita Kala, screenwriter and author, joining me on this broadcast.
Professor Badri Narayan is a columnist and political analyst.
Sanjay Kumar is co-director, Lokniti CSDS, joining us on this broadcast.
Welcome.
Advaita Kala, the Prime Minister's 76th birthday.
There are so many aspects to talk about, closest to my heart, national security, Article 370, the Divya Bhavya Ram Mandir at Ayodhya.
There is so much to talk about.
Absolutely so much, so much to talk about and you know like you mentioned what's close to your heart.
I think what's close to my heart about the Prime Minister is his eternal optimism, no matter what the challenges, no matter how difficult the journey is.
The one thing that the prime minister has in his approach to all issues is just this unbreakable optimism.
And that's just something that we can learn as individuals, whether you are politically aligned with his party or not.
I just think that approach to life, to living, and the kind of achievements that can happen because of that attitude to life
is worth learning from the Prime Minister because his journey is not only one about political office.
It is a journey that started in a poor home at a tea stall in Vardnagar and has traveled such a great distance socially.
He's an OBC.

No, so just imagine that young boy from Vadnagar amongst the tallest leaders in the world today, Anand Ranganathan, if we were to talk about, you know, even when world leaders stand together or talk together,

heading the fastest growing large economy prime minister for 12 years and counting you know and such huge constituencies and such a big country he stands tall even in the world where people had said foreign policy will be very difficult for him when he became prime minister in 2014.
Good evening, Gaurav, and good evening to my fellow panellists.
And of course, congratulations to our Prime Minister Modi for his 76th birthday.
I wish him very well, as does the entire nation and perhaps the world as well, of course.
Look, as the movie of my namesake, Anand said, and I think that is what, in some measure, I would hope, and I think Mr. Modi also believes his life service should be,
I would say he's halfway there.
He's done some incredible job, you know, things for India in the last 11, 12 years.
But there is so much to do that I just, you know, as an Indian who loves this country and everyone else does, I'm just not satisfied with the pace with which things are moving.
They are moving in the right direction.
There are some incredible achievements of his, the most notable being vaccinating one billion Indians
twice over within one year, which is incredible, the other being, you know, national security-wise.
So, there are things that are going spectacularly right.

But there are also things that are, I would say, possibly alarming in the sense that, if we want Viksit Bharat by 2047, we just aren't or he just isn't taking those difficult decisions that would make us achieve that
pedestal that everyone in his party and everyone seems to be talking about.
Because at the end of the day, if I can just 20, 30 seconds, I'll tell you, encapsulate where things are not moving in the direction I would want them to move.
In order for us to become Vixit Bharat by 2047, we want a healthier, wealthier, wiser, more flexible workforce.
And we just don't have that in any of those compartments right now.
When you talk of healthier, 34% of Indian infants under five are chronically malnourished and stunted.
When you talk of wealthier, our GDP per capita is lower than Sri Lanka ranked 140.
When you talk of wiser, 50 million Indian children are out of school.
And when you talk of flexibility, 44% of our workforce is involved in agriculture that contributes only 14% GDP.
So there are so many things wrong.
I didn't want to have a laundry list of things that are wrong.
I want to congratulate him for the things that he's done right.
And I hope that he would make the tough decisions, the tough reforms that are needed for us to achieve that developed country by 2047.
Oh, you're absolutely right.
There's a lot that needs to be done, a lot that has been done.
The pace needs to be much faster.
And he's promised the nation a faster pace.
What makes him click?

politically is a question that we will go to Sanjay Bhai for but for a moment I quickly want to cut across to Varanasi, you know from Vadnagar now we talk about Varanasi, his constituency and a lot happening in Varanasi that's now sent him to parliament three times.
Well, exactly, Gaurav, if you can hear me, I'm present at the Namoghat and it's the birthday of Prime Minister of India and the MP of Varanasi, Narendra Modi.

such Dhyas you have seen in Ayodhya's Dipotsav, but no it's not Dipotsav, it's the birthday.

So he has the ability to galvanize what works for the Prime Minister election after election Sanjay Kumar as co-director Lokniti CSDS as a Syphologist you've studied the Prime Minister what's been working for him first in Gujarat and then at the national scale Kiran Rijiju just said that even if it's a panchayat election the vote is for him even if it's a Lok Sabha election it's in his name
The list is very long, Gaurav.
It's not one thing which is working in his favor.
There is no doubt that he is a very popular leader.
He is far more popular than any other leader.
But if I need to mention a few things, what makes him so popular among the people of this country, among the voters of this country, a few things to just name.
One, he's an honest leader, and that's a big asset any political leader has.
An honest decision-maker, a strong leader, the one who has lifted India's image in the world.
So these are four or five things which makes him absolutely stand-alone compared to any other leader.
decision-maker and a strong leader.
That's one of the big assets and I'm going and I'm saying this based on the surveys which we have been doing.
Year after year, whenever we do the survey, these are the few things which come to people's minds that why he's popular, because he's a strong leader, he takes decision,
and he is an honest leader, so these are the few things.

Indeed, Rajat Sethi, you know even on the world stage, he's now one of the senior leaders on the world stage, Prime Minister for 12 years and counting, but a decision maker, he's faced global headwinds, you know 2014 onwards and specially we were to talk about, you know
2020 COVID, he faced the Russia-Ukraine war, the war between Israel, Iran and the United States of America.
So global headwinds that impacted global economy, but he's been able to steer the ship as steadily as possible.
Well, Gaurav, I think rarely any Indian leader would have had to face so many headwinds, be it COVID, be it two or three wars, and then reforms that had to be done, which were painstakingly hard.
And it's not easy to reform a country as big as India.
And he has invested a lot of his political capital to see the country through.
And this is one nature which we all, when he was elected in 2014, we looked up to.
I mean, I remember my—I was graduating in the U.S.
And in all likelihood, I was about to stay in the U.S.
But when this leader dawned upon India, there was one rare glimmer of hope that country can actually withstand all kinds of challenges.
And there is some hope.
And this is the reason why several scores and scores of people came back to the country in the hope that we'll all work towards the larger cause.
And I think this is one place, especially when it comes to the global setting where India was and where India is today, one thing that even his detractors will have to agree upon
is that he has elevated India's image worldwide.
This is as objective a fact as it can get.
Even the Congress folks, all his opponents, political opponents, would believe, will have to believe this.

Even today, the Canadian prime minister, I mean, in a random conversation that he was having globally on energy crisis, he had to praise prime minister because of his leadership in ensuring that the markets remain calm.

And, I mean, anecdotes after anecdotes go about where his leadership on the international level, not just the India's country level, but on an international level, he has garnered respect from his contemporaries around the world.
He has withstood on the ground where India's interests concern.
And he has also presented a very interesting moral perspective
in a new sense, in a new redefined sense, which was largely missing in the years in the run up to when he became the prime minister.
And one thing is very clear, I mean, he's not embarrassed about telling the world that he's putting India's interests first.
that he is here, he is prime minister of India and Indian interests matter a maximum to him, everything else is secondary to that.
But Professor Badri Narayan, you know Dr Sanjay Kumar was talking about how report after report seems to indicate that people still react

positively to the Prime Minister, you know he spoke of his honesty, decision making, lifted India's image globally and multiple other factors but do you see that often, I mean as a professor, you've studied political leaders, after some years people get bored, people start looking for alternatives, is the Prime Minister anywhere close to reaching that stage that people start looking for alternatives or he continues to go strong in your view?
Gaurav, I think one of the capacity of Modi Ji is he always reinvent himself and he always comes with a new posturing in the politics.
So there is no issue of boring with him.
Because he always reinvent, comes with a new kind of engagement, new form of the discourse, new politics.
So that kind of thing he does.
So there is no issue of boring.
But, you know, every birthday pose some challenges.
So you have to resolve the challenges.
And, you know, India is a country which is facing a lot of challenge.
And for a leader like Modi Ji, he is trying to resolve problems in his own ways.
Like you see, the entire, the speed of social mobility is very fast in India.
The Gareeb Kalyan Yojana, through the Gareeb Kalyan policies, 25 crore people moved from Povachi to the lower class, lower class to the middle class.
So, a lot of, at various structures, mobility is faster.
Secondly, what he did, Gaurav, he gave a new way of doing politics of the state, linked with the issue of social, like social politics.
Every issue he links with the social issue, like even this birthday celebration, you see it is linked with the seva sankalp.
So, a lot of blood donations, this and that.
So, a lot of SEWA and the social empowerment policies he brings with every political act.
So, politics is not for politics of the state and the election, like Ban Ki Bar.
So, through various ways, he's tried to approach the social issues and link the social issues with the politics, and we used to do social politics.

And it's interesting you said that he's constantly trying to reinvent himself and remain relevant even to future generations and we'll talk about that because when you look at those images of the Prime Minister interacting not just with those who are turning 18 or Gen Z but also interacting with those who will be voters subsequently and we'll come to that point with Advaita in just a moment.
